concept.title: Chicago Manual of Style (CMOS)
concept.shortdesc: The Chicago Manual of Style (CMOS) is a general‑purpose style guide used heavily in publishing,

conbody.p:
The Chicago Manual of Style (CMOS) is a general‑purpose style guide used heavily in publishing, academia, and many technical‑publishing environments that value formal prose and citation consistency. When used in technical writing, CMOS‑aligned documentation tends to:
Follow traditional English style rules for punctuation, spelling variants, and capitalization, often chosen for readability to a broad (including non‑technical) audience.
Use note‑and‑bibliography or author–date citation schemes, which are useful when the documentation cites external research, standards, or regulatory material.

In many organizations, CMOS is used in parallel with a more technical or in‑house guide (for example, for legal, regulatory, or marketing‑facing content), while simpler UI‑facing help follows a more minimal, command‑oriented style.
